# DECISIONS — Make working in the Live Work Surface feel safe

## How I approached this
I read LiveWorkSurface.tsx and the two session routes first, then prompted my
model in pieces: first to enumerate loss modes in the component as it stood,
then to implement the fix I picked, then to fold in the mid-flight
flaky-connection note, then to sanity-check the result. I did not run
typecheck/tests in this pass — I read the generated diff carefully and trust
well-iterated output over a formal check I didn't have time for.

## Loss modes identified (from the "list the loss modes" prompt)
1. **Tab close / refresh / crash** — `files`, `name`, `contact` and any event
   in `pendingRef` live only in React state + a ref. Nothing is written to disk
   or localStorage. Closing the tab a second after a big edit loses that edit
   AND everything typed since the last successful 8s flush.
2. **The 8-second flush window itself** — even with a healthy connection, up
   to `FLUSH_MS` (8s) of edits are only ever "at risk" in memory before they
   reach the server.
3. **No restore path** — even if the server DID have every event, the page
   never reads it back on mount. A reload always starts from the pristine
   seed, not from where the candidate left off. This makes (1) permanent
   instead of recoverable.
4. **Network failures during flush** — the existing code already re-buffers
   an unsent batch (nice), but a failed flush was silent — no indication to
   the candidate that anything was wrong, and no faster retry than "wait for
   the next interval."
5. **Multi-tab** — opening the same token in two tabs races two independent
   sessions. Real, but rarer and lower-stakes than (1)-(3); explicitly
   deprioritized (see below).

## Loss mode I prioritized: (1) + (3), the "tab close / refresh loses
## everything" combo
This is the one every candidate can hit by accident (fat-fingering Ctrl+W,
the browser's own crash-restore not applying because this is a `textarea`
inside client state, a laptop sleeping mid-case) and, before this change, it
was **unrecoverable** — there was no code path that ever read a session back.
That combination (common trigger + total, permanent loss) made it the highest
expected-value fix within a 1.5h box, ahead of tightening the flush interval
or dealing with multi-tab.

## Implementation
`app/devcase/apply/[token]/LiveWorkSurface.tsx`:
- Every meaningful mutation (edit keystroke, file open, paste, decision-log
  edit, name/contact change) now also writes a snapshot
  (`files`, `pending` events, `sessionId`, `name`, `contact`) to
  `localStorage` under a per-token key, synchronously, in addition to the
  existing debounced server flush. This is deliberately **not** debounced —
  localStorage writes are cheap and this is the layer that has to survive an
  unload event that gives us no time to wait.
- On mount, before rendering the pristine seed, the component checks
  localStorage for that token and restores from it if present (files, active
  path, identity fields, unflushed events, session id). A small "Restored
  your in-progress work from this browser" notice tells the candidate it
  happened instead of leaving it invisible.
- `submit()` only clears the localStorage entry once the server has
  *confirmed* the submission — an error leaves the local copy in place so a
  retry (or a reload after the error) doesn't start blank.

## Mid-flight update reaction (flaky/offline connections, minutes-long)
When the "hotel/train wifi, offline for a few minutes, not an edge case"
note came in, I had already built the localStorage layer above — which
turns out to be exactly the right foundation, since it makes the browser
(not the server round-trip) the source of truth for "is my work safe." I
went back and re-prompted for the network-facing half:
- `flush()` now checks `navigator.onLine` and skips the network attempt
  entirely when the browser already knows it's offline, instead of letting
  fetches fail one by one every 8 seconds against a connection that isn't
  there.
- Added `online`/`offline` listeners: the moment connectivity returns, we
  flush immediately rather than waiting out the rest of the poll interval —
  the gap matters most right after a multi-minute drop, where "up to 8
  more seconds" would otherwise become "up to 8 seconds after the candidate
  already noticed wifi is back."
- Added a small `syncState` indicator (`Saved.` / `Saving…` / `Offline —
  your work is saved on this device and will sync automatically.`) so the
  candidate isn't left guessing during a long dead spot — the message is
  intentionally reassuring rather than alarming, because the work genuinely
  is safe locally at that point.
- Added a best-effort flush on `visibilitychange`/`pagehide` (tab
  backgrounded or closed) as a bonus — but I did not lean on it for
  correctness, since on a flaky connection it can fail exactly when it
  matters most. localStorage is the real guarantee; the network flush is
  now best-effort at every layer, which is the correct posture once you
  take "offline for minutes" seriously instead of "offline for an instant
  during a request."

## Rejected alternatives
- **IndexedDB / a service worker for true offline queueing.** More robust
  and the "correct" long-term answer, but a bigger surface than the timebox
  allows and overkill for a text-file-sized payload; localStorage's ~5MB
  ceiling and synchronous API are more than sufficient here. Revisit if
  seed files grow much larger.
- **Shortening `FLUSH_MS` (8s → e.g. 2s) instead of adding local
  persistence.** Would reduce the *server-side* at-risk window but does
  nothing for a reload/crash (state still starts from the seed) and nothing
  for an offline stretch (more frequent failed fetches, not fewer). Treated
  as a non-fix for the loss mode I prioritized, so I didn't touch it.
- **A server-side GET endpoint to restore from the DB instead of
  localStorage.** Would also solve "resume on a different device," which is
  strictly more capable, but requires a new API route plus auth/consistency
  handling for a candidate-controlled session id, and doesn't help at all
  during the exact offline window the mid-flight update called out (no
  network → no GET either). localStorage covers the reload/crash case
  including with no connection, which is the scenario in play; cross-device
  resume is a reasonable v2 if it turns out to matter.
- **Clearing localStorage on every successful flush (not just on
  submit).** Would keep the stored payload minimal, but reintroduces exactly
  the loss mode being fixed: a flush can succeed and then the tab can close
  before the *next* edit is flushed, and if the local copy had already been
  cleared there's nothing to restore. Local storage is kept authoritative
  until a *confirmed submit*, not until "server currently agrees."
- **Blocking submit while offline with a clearer message ("you're offline,
  try again").** `canSubmit`/`submit()` were left mostly as-is; an offline
  submit attempt still surfaces the existing generic error state. I judged
  a bespoke offline-submit message as polish beyond the 1.5h box once the
  bigger loss mode (silent, permanent data loss) was closed — noted here so
  it isn't mistaken for an oversight.
- **Multi-tab conflict handling** (last-write-wins races between two tabs
  on the same token) — out of scope; rare compared to the single-tab loss
  modes above, and the existing "last flush wins" behavior isn't made worse
  by this change.
- **i18n for the new UI strings** ("Restored your in-progress work…",
  "Saved." / "Saving…" / "Offline — …"). Left as plain English literals
  rather than going through `next-intl` message files, to keep the change
  small and fast within the timebox; every other string in this component
  goes through `t()`/`tApply()`, so this is a known, deliberate inconsistency
  a follow-up should clean up (add `devApply.workSurface.sync*` keys across
  `messages/*.json`).

chat.text: I'm looking at LiveWorkSurface.tsx (in-browser editor for a dev-case). List every way in-progress work in this component can actually be lost - be concrete about the trigger for each, not generic advice.

Five loss modes: (1) tab close/refresh/crash - files/name/contact/pendingRef live only in React state+refs, nothing persisted; (2) the FLUSH_MS=8000 window - up to 8s of edits at risk even on a good connection; (3) no restore path at all - even server-side history is never read back on mount, so a reload always starts from the pristine seed; (4) a failed flush is silently re-buffered with no indication to the user and no faster retry; (5) two tabs on the same token race independent sessions. #1+#3 together are the worst: common trigger, and currently unrecoverable.

Agreed, #1+#3 is the one to fix. Give me a plan for a client-side local-first autosave: persist the editable file tree + identity fields + not-yet-flushed events to localStorage keyed by token, restore it on mount before falling back to the seed. Don't touch the server/API yet.

Plan: add storageKeyFor(token), a persistLocal() that snapshots {files, pending, name, contact, sessionId} synchronously to localStorage, call it from record()/onEdit()/name+contact handlers. On mount, one effect reads the key before the seed renders, restores files/activePath/identity/pendingRef/sessionId if present, sets a restoredNotice flag. Only clear the key on a confirmed submit so an error retry doesn't start blank.

Write that: persistLocal, the restore-on-mount effect, and wire persistLocal into record() and onEdit(). Keep it synchronous, no debounce on the localStorage write itself - the debounce that already exists is for the server flush, don't touch that.
[implementation pasted: persistLocal callback + refs for name/contact + restore effect reading localStorage before first paint + persistLocal() calls added inside record() and onEdit()]
Good. Now also wire it into the name/contact TextInput onChange handlers, and clear the stored entry only when submit() gets a real 200 back, not just when we attempt it.
[implementation pasted: onChange handlers now update the ref + call persistLocal(); submit() only calls localStorage.removeItem after ok is true, inside a try/catch]
One more before I move on - add a small visible notice when we restore from localStorage on mount, something like 'restored your work from this browser', not just a silent recovery.
Added a restoredNotice boolean set in the mount effect and a small banner rendered under the note/heading when it's true.

[team update relayed] a meaningful share of candidates are on flaky connections - hotel/train wifi, offline for a few minutes at a stretch, not a rare edge case. whatever we ship has to tolerate that.

New constraint just came in: treat multi-minute offline stretches as normal, not exceptional. My localStorage layer already makes the browser the source of truth, so content loss is basically covered - but the flush/network code still just retries blindly every 8s and gives the user zero feedback. Rework flush() to check navigator.onLine and skip the network attempt when offline instead of failing repeatedly, add online/offline listeners so we resync immediately the instant connectivity returns rather than waiting out the interval, and add a small synced/saving/offline indicator in the UI.

[implementation pasted: flush() now short-circuits on navigator.onLine===false and sets syncState; online/offline window listeners, the online one triggers an immediate flush; a syncState-driven indicator renders Saved / Saving / Offline - your work is saved on this device and will sync automatically.]
Also add a best-effort flush on visibilitychange/pagehide for the backgrounded-tab case, but make clear in a comment that it's a bonus, not the safety net - localStorage is.

Added visibilitychange + pagehide listeners calling flush with submit:false, with a comment noting it's best-effort; localStorage via persistLocal remains the durable guarantee regardless of whether this fires or the request completes.
Read the whole file back to me - I want to sanity-check the ordering of setFiles/filesRef/persistLocal in onEdit, I don't fully trust that the ref is current before persistLocal reads it.

onEdit's setFiles updater now assigns filesRef.current = next synchronously inside the updater before returning next, so the persistLocal() call right after reads the up-to-date ref rather than the stale pre-edit value - the effect-based sync (filesRef.current = files) alone would lag a render behind, which is why the updater does it inline.

notes: Prioritized the tab-close/refresh loss mode (unrecoverable pre-fix) with a synchronous localStorage local-first layer, then reworked the network layer for tolerance of multi-minute offline stretches once the flaky-wifi update landed; verification was reading the diff back carefully rather than running typecheck or tests.
